ballot: Democrats win the House — Minority Leader Jeffries projects 255+ seats, the largest Democratic majority since 2009 (CBS News, NBC News, Nov. 3–4, 2026)
approval: 38% in Election Day exit polls — among the lowest on record for a midterm president (NBC News exit polls, Nov. 3, 2026)
ledger_source: CBS News, NBC News, The Hill, Newsweek and Mississippi Free Press election-night and day-after reporting, Nov. 3–5, 2026

headlines.headline: Democrats seize the House — and the knives come out in both parties
headlines.summary: CBS projects Democrats have won House control; Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries says the party will hold at least 255 seats, its largest majority since 2009, with leadership elections set for Nov. 18-19. Speaker Mike Johnson won't seek the minority leader post, touching off a fight between Jim Jordan and Steve Scalise, while incoming Oversight Chair Robert Garcia has outlined investigations into Trump family business dealings, DHS/ICE and the Epstein files. Notable GOP losses include Reps. David Valadao (CA-22), Tom Barrett (MI-7), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1) and Kevin Kiley (CA-6).

headlines.headline: El-Sayed flips Michigan's Senate seat
headlines.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers to win Michigan's open Senate seat, one of the marquee Democratic pickups of the night and a boost for the party's progressive wing.

headlines.headline: Talarico routs Paxton in Texas
headlines.summary: Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton for Texas's Senate seat by a wide 55%-43% margin (about 1.2 million votes) with all precincts reporting — a result Fox News described conservative reaction to as a "catastrophic" and "blue tsunami" night, with Sen. Ted Cruz calling it a "Watergate-level repudiation."

headlines.headline: Alaska Senate race still too close to call — but the majority's already decided
headlines.summary: Democrats have already secured Senate control regardless of the outcome, but Alaska remains a nail-biter: Democrat Mary Peltola led Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan 48.2% to 47.9% as of midweek, with a ranked-choice tabulation that may not be finished before certification, targeted for Nov. 25. A Peltola win would be Democrats' first Alaska Senate pickup since 2014.

headlines.headline: Mississippi Senate race down to about 1,100 votes
headlines.summary: Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by roughly 1,100-1,800 votes depending on the tracker, in a race nobody expected to be close. Thousands of affidavit and absentee ballots remain outstanding; Harrison County won't finish counting its affidavits until Nov. 10.

podcasts.summary: "Dems win big in midterm elections" (Nov 4) — NPR's team breaks down the scale of the House and Senate flips the morning after.
"Holy crap, what an election!" (Nov 4) — a race-by-race rundown of the night's biggest upsets, including Texas, Michigan and the still-uncalled Alaska and Mississippi Senate contests.
"The world is reacting to the Democrats' sweeping midterm elections victory" (Nov 4) — international reaction and what the result signals for Trump's remaining two years.

wildcard: Democrats have won a majority of U.S. governorships for the first time in 16 years, flipping five Trump-won states (Georgia, Ohio, Texas, Iowa and Nevada) in a single night.
